documents.title: Visiting Hours & Visitor Policy
documents.text: General wards: visiting hours 10:00-20:00, maximum 2 visitors per bedside. ICU: 12:00-14:00 and 18:00-19:00, maximum 2 visitors. End-of-life care: unrestricted visiting per KB-12. Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult and cleared by the charge nurse. Visitors with infectious symptoms must not enter wards.

documents.title: Sepsis Screening & Activation (qSOFA)
documents.text: Screen every admitted patient with suspected infection using qSOFA: respiratory rate >= 22/min, systolic BP <= 100 mmHg, altered mentation (GCS < 15). qSOFA >= 2: activate the Sepsis Six within 1 hour - take blood cultures, measure serum lactate, administer broad-spectrum antibiotics after cultures, begin 30 mL/kg crystalloid for hypotension, monitor urine output, give high-flow oxygen as needed.

documents.title: Metformin Renal Dosing
documents.text: Metformin dosing by eGFR: eGFR >= 45 - standard dosing permitted. eGFR 30-44 - maximum 1000 mg/day, do not initiate new patients. eGFR < 30 - CONTRAINDICATED, stop metformin and switch agents. Hold metformin before iodinated contrast and for 48 h after in patients with eGFR 30-60.

documents.title: Return to Activity After Myocardial Infarction
documents.text: After STEMI: supervised walking by week 2, structured cardiac rehabilitation from week 4. Competitive sport requires cardiology assessment no earlier than 3 months post-MI plus functional imaging (stress echo or perfusion scan). Driving: 1 week for non-commercial license, 4 weeks for professional drivers (DVLA guidance adopted).

documents.title: Neonatal Medication Safety
documents.text: All neonatal doses must be weight-based (mg/kg), double-checked by two credentialed staff, and verified by pharmacy before administration. Adult formulations must never be used on the neonatal unit. High-alert medications (insulin, heparin, opioids) require independent double-check and smart-pump programming.

documents.title: Chest Pain Triage (STEMI Pathway)
documents.text: Crushing chest pain > 20 minutes, radiating to jaw or arm, with diaphoresis or nausea: activate the STEMI pathway - ECG within 10 minutes of arrival, door-to-balloon target <= 90 minutes, aspirin 300 mg chewed unless contraindicated, troponin on arrival and at 3 hours. Do not discharge chest pain as anxiety without documented workup (ECG + troponin).

documents.title: Patient Privacy & PHI Handling
documents.text: Staff must apply the minimum-necessary principle: access only records of patients under their care. Patient identifiers (name, MRN, DOB) must never be echoed into non-clinical systems, logs, or General Purpose AI tooling. When using internal AI assistants, submit clinical questions WITHOUT patient identifiers; use 'the patient' phrasing instead. Violations are reportable to the privacy officer.

documents.title: Antibiotic Stewardship & Penicillin Allergy
documents.text: Documented penicillin allergy: avoid amoxicillin and other beta-lactams unless allergy de-labeling is complete. Documented anaphylaxis to penicillin: use vancomycin or aztreonam per ID consult for serious infections; for pharyngitis use azithromycin or clarithromycin. Always verify allergy history before prescribing; never rely on patient recall alone for anaphylaxis history.

documents.title: Iodinated Contrast Allergy Premedication
documents.text: Prior mild reaction (hives, itching): premedicate with prednisone 50 mg PO at 13, 7, and 1 hour before contrast, plus diphenhydramine 50 mg 1 hour before. Prior anaphylaxis to iodinated contrast: do not premedicate and proceed - use alternative imaging (MRI, ultrasound) or obtain allergy/ID consult. Document the reaction history in the imaging request.

documents.title: VTE Prophylaxis (Padua Score)
documents.text: Assess VTE risk on admission with the Padua score. Score >= 4: high risk - start pharmacologic prophylaxis with LMWH (enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily) unless contraindicated (active bleeding, platelets < 50, recent neurosurgery). Score < 4: mechanical prophylaxis and reassess at 24 h and on any clinical change.

documents.title: Discharge Documentation Standards
documents.text: Discharge summaries must be completed within 24 hours of discharge and include: confirmed diagnosis, medication reconciliation with changes explained, follow-up appointments (within 7 days for high-risk patients), red-flag symptoms with return instructions, and results pending at discharge. Copy to the GP within 48 hours.

documents.title: ICU Visiting Exceptions (End of Life)
documents.text: For patients in the end-of-life phase as documented by the attending: visiting is unrestricted, 24 hours, including during procedures if the family wishes. Family conference room ICU-2 is available; notify the charge nurse to arrange overnight accommodation for next of kin.
